title: Carbon monoxide alarm
note: The sensor wears out, and many units sound an end-of-life chirp. Check the date on the back and replace on schedule.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Dryer vent (plastic)
note: Plastic or foil flex duct traps lint and is a fire risk. Replace it with rigid or semi-rigid metal duct.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Caulking (interior and exterior)
note: Cracked or pulled-away caulk lets water in around windows, trim and tubs. It is cheap to redo and prevents costly rot.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Washing machine
note: Wide range because use varies. Leaks, violent shaking and rust-colored water mean it is failing; check the supply hoses and drain pan.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Tank water heater
note: Mineral-rich water shortens life. Rust at the base, moisture in the pan or rumbling mean it is failing, and a burst tank can flood the area, so replace one past its range before it leaks.

sources.publisher: US Department of Energy, Energy Saver Guide (2022)
sources.quote: Most storage water heaters last 10-15 years, while tankless water heaters can last more than 20 years.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Sump pump
note: It only matters when it rains hard, so test it before storm season by pouring water in the pit. A battery backup helps if the power fails.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Exterior paint
note: Surface preparation and paint quality matter most; sun shortens life. Peeling and chalking mean it is due before the wood underneath is exposed.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Central air conditioner
note: Hot or coastal climates and neglected filters shorten life. Weak cooling, ice on the lines and frequent repairs are the signs.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Carpet
note: Traffic and cleaning set the life. Matting, stains that return and worn backing mean it is done.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Dishwasher
note: Hard water and heavy use shorten life. Leaks at the door and rust in the tub are the signs.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Refrigerator
note: Dusty coils and worn door seals shorten life. Frost, warm spots and a constantly running compressor suggest trouble.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Smoke alarm
note: Replace a smoke alarm when it fails to respond to testing, or every 10 years, whichever comes first. The manufacture date is printed on the back.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI, Smoke Alarm Inspection
sources.quote: Smoke alarms should be replaced when they fail to respond to testing, or every 10 years, whichever is sooner.

title: Garage door opener
note: Quality and how often it is used set the life. Test the auto-reverse by laying a board on the floor under the door; an opener that fails to reverse needs replacing.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Heat pump
note: A heat pump runs for both heating and cooling. Yearly service and clean coils help.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Tankless water heater
note: Scale buildup from hard water is the main enemy; periodic descaling helps it reach the long end. Sources differ widely, so treat the range as a guide.

sources.publisher: US Department of Energy, Energy Saver Guide (2022)
sources.quote: Most storage water heaters last 10-15 years, while tankless water heaters can last more than 20 years.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Deck framing
note: Check for hidden rot where the ledger meets the house and at the posts. A deck that bounces or sways should be checked before anyone uses it.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Garbage disposal
note: Jams, leaks under the sink and a motor that hums are the signs.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Clothes dryer
note: Lint buildup is a fire hazard whatever the age; clean the lint trap every load and the vent duct regularly.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Electric range
note: Burner elements and switches can be replaced, so age alone is not a reason to scrap it. Scorched or cracked elements should be replaced.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Well pump
note: Sediment and frequent cycling shorten life. Short cycling, low pressure or spitting air mean the pump or pressure tank is in trouble.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Wood deck boards
note: Sun and moisture decide it. Soft spots, splitting and loose boards are the sign.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Gas range
note: Burners and igniters wear first.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Aluminum windows
note: Corroded tracks and failed seals are common. They also conduct heat and cold, so old ones are costly to run.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Asphalt driveway
note: Cracks let water in, which freezing then widens. Sealing and crack repair extend the life.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Faucets and spray hose
note: Drips and stiff handles mean worn cartridges or seals. A fix is usually cheap.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Flat roof (EPDM rubber)
note: Seams, edges and penetrations leak first. Ponding water and punctures from foot traffic shorten life.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes
sources.quote: EPDM (ethylene propylene diene monomer) Rubber 15 to 25

title: Forced-air furnace
note: Cracks in the heat exchanger can leak carbon monoxide, so have an older furnace checked yearly and keep a working CO alarm nearby. Frequent repairs and rising bills are signs of age.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Septic system
note: Regular pumping and inspection extend life; the drainfield usually fails first. Slow drains, odors and wet or unusually green ground over the drainfield are the warning signs.

sources.publisher: US EPA, New Homebuyer's Guide to Septic Systems
sources.quote: The average lifespan of a septic system is 15 to 40 years, but it can last longer if properly maintained!

title: Asphalt shingle roof (3-tab)
note: Hot climates can shorten asphalt shingle life. Curling, cracked or bald shingles and granules in the gutters mean it is near the end.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Flat roof (modified bitumen)
note: Cracked or blistered surfaces and open seams mean water is getting in. Keep drains clear so water does not pool.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Water softener
note: Salt bridges and resin wear reduce performance. Hard-water scale returning means it needs service.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Garage door
note: Springs and cables wear with every use. A door that sticks, sags or looks off-balance should be serviced by a pro, since springs under tension can injure.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Aluminum gutters and downspouts
note: Sagging, leaking seams and water spilling over the edge are the signs. Failed gutters send water to the foundation.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes
sources.quote: Aluminum Gutters, Downspouts, Soffit and Fascia 20 to 40+

title: Vinyl or fiberglass windows
note: Fogging between panes means the seal has failed. Warped frames and drafts are other signs.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Vinyl floor
note: Curling seams and cracks let water reach the subfloor. Very old sheet vinyl can contain asbestos, so do not sand it.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Wood shake roof
note: Moss, rot and splitting shorten life. Wood roofs also burn more readily than most, so check local fire rules before replacing like for like.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Asphalt shingle roof (architectural)
note: Thicker laminated shingles last longer, but heat, hail and severe storms can cut that short. Ask for the roof's install date.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: GFCI outlets
note: The chart says up to 30 years. Press the test button monthly; one that will not trip or reset must be replaced.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Wood windows
note: The chart says 30+ years. Paint and sealant upkeep decides it: peeling paint and soft sills mean rot is starting.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Boiler (hot-water or steam)
note: Boilers can outlast furnaces by many years. Leaks around the unit, rust and rising pressure problems suggest it is wearing out.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Concrete walkway
note: The chart lists walks, not driveways. Heaved or cracked slabs are a trip hazard worth fixing.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Metal roof
note: Life depends on the metal and coating. Loose fasteners and flashing are usually what fail first, not the panels.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Chimney flue tile
note: A cracked liner can let heat and fumes reach the framing. Have the chimney inspected before using the fireplace in an older house.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Cast-iron drain pipe (below ground)
note: Old cast-iron drains rust from the inside. Repeated backups and slow drains in a house of this age are worth a camera inspection.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Copper water supply lines
note: Acidic water and high pressure shorten life. Green stains and pinhole leaks are the warning signs.

InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Electrical service panel
note: Age matters less than the brand and condition. Rust, scorch marks, buzzing or warm breakers mean call an electrician.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Vinyl siding
note: Siding rarely fails from age; look for cracks, warping and loose panels that let water behind it.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Heating and cooling ductwork
note: Ducts outlast the equipment but leak at joints over time. Dust streaks, uneven rooms and high bills point to leaks.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Clay or concrete tile roof
note: The tile itself can last a century or more (the chart says 100+). The underlayment beneath often wears out first, so cracked or slipped tiles are the warning sign.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Fiber cement siding
note: The chart says 100+. Keep the paint sound and the bottom edges clear of soil and splashing water.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Fiberglass exterior door
note: The chart gives 100+ years for fiberglass doors. The weatherstripping wears out every five to eight years, so a draft means new seals, not a new door.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes
InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes
sources.quote: The gaskets/weatherstripping of exterior doors may have to be replaced every five to eight years.

title: Hardwood floor
note: Solid wood can be refinished several times and lasts for the life of the house (the chart says 100+). Water damage is what ends it.

sources.publisher: InterNACHI Standard Estimated Life Expectancy Chart for Homes

title: Toilets
note: The china bowl lasts (the chart says 100+). The tank parts wear out in about five years, so a running toilet is a cheap repair.
